rationale: Two preceding completed full reader jobs took1313.477 and1378.679 seconds from their first runner log to cleanup, including successful full registry refresh and Chromium validation; both were superseded and did not deploy.

The cdb job used707.131 seconds before starting full refresh and then ran that refresh for at least1104.632 seconds before generic cancellation at1811.763 seconds overall. The current30-minute build cap therefore offers little or no headroom under the observed slower run.

The45-minute bounded allowance adds15 minutes to the complete build job. Using the cancelled run’s observed pre-refresh duration, it leaves about1992.869 seconds for full refresh, browser verification and guarded synchronization. This is headroom, not a claimed successful45-minute runtime.

Only the main-branch build job cap changes. Existing PR validation remains30 minutes and deployment remains15 minutes. All commands, source budgets and pacing, branch checks, permissions, concurrency, full software/source/browser validation and exact-head publication guards remain byte-identical.
The current5749 run already started with the original30-minute workflow. This patch affects subsequent runs and does not extend, cancel or rerun the existing job.
